title: August 2026 fresh-intake production - batch H3B-2, the Snapshot-01 technical queue
note: FOUR TECHNICAL ROOTS, FOUR NEW CARDS, AND ONE IDENTITY LEFT OPEN. LOCAL CORPUS FIRST, AND IT PAID. Three of the four roots were answered from instruments already held. MARPOL Annex VI regulation 16 came from MEPC.328(76) in the shared corpus, and the corpus's own frozen canonical record MARPOLVI_REG16.json supplied the currentness statement outright - 'REGULATION 16 IS UNAMENDED ... its current consolidated text is therefore identical to the base text adopted by MEPC.328(76), in force 2023-11-01'. MARPOL Annex I regulation 31 came from MEPC.117(52), and the held Annex I amendment chain confirmed none of them touches reg. 31. MLC Regulation 3.2 and Standard A3.2 came from mlc-2006.pdf. Only where the local corpora were genuinely silent was anything retrieved. WHAT THE CORPUS COULD NOT ANSWER, AND WHY IT MATTERED. Regulation 31 contains NO calibration interval - it requires the system to be approved by the Administration and installed per 'the guidelines and specifications developed by the Organization'. Those guidelines were not held, so the ODMCS calibration question was unanswerable from the corpus. MEPC.108(49) and MEPC.240(65) were retrieved from IMO's resolution index, read, and preserved into the affected instrument's folder. Section 5.3 is the answer: accuracy 'should be verified at the IOPP renewal surveys' and 'the calibration certificate certifying date of last calibration check should be retained on board for inspection purposes'. The card therefore states plainly that there is no MARPOL interval and gives what actually applies instead, which is what section 12 of the brief required. A NOTES FILE IS NOT A SOURCE, AND IT HAD ALREADY COST US. The PMS root needed IACS authority. The corpus area 07-iacs-and-class held only CLASS_AND_SURVEY_NOTES.md - a note asserting what a Unified Requirement says, not the requirement. IACS's own consolidated UR Z document was retrieved and preserved, and its contents page settled the question: Z7 is 'Hull classification surveys', Z18 is 'Survey of machinery', Z20 is 'Planned maintenance scheme (PMS) for machinery', Z27 is condition-based maintenance. THE ORAL BANK WAS WRONG: QB1_supplementary#q4 attributed Continuous Machinery Survey to 'IACS UR Z7/Z7.1' in four places. That is corrected in this batch under CORR-URZ7-01. The defect had been in the product since before this session and was only exposed because a new card needed the real citation - which is the general lesson: an unsourced area of the corpus does not announce its own errors. THE ANSWER TO AUG-0225 IS A VERBATIM QUOTATION. UR Z20 2.3.1: 'When the PMS is approved a "Certificate of Approval for Planned Maintenance Scheme" is issued. However, other equivalent certification or class notation may be issued according to the procedure in use in each individual Member Society. In any case, the certification is to be kept on board.' Section 10 of the brief required that this be identified as CLASS and not presented as a statutory IMO certificate, and required the company PMS under ISM section 10 to be distinguished from the class-approved survey arrangement. Both are done in the first two sentences of the card. INTERPRETATION OF THE FRESH-WATER ROOT, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Section 9 warned against assuming boiler chemistry. It also cuts the other way, so the reading is justified on evidence rather than asserted: AUG-0223 sits on a Nair and Srivastava panel between a ballast-water treatment approval question and an engine-room documentation question, and asks what the CHIEF ENGINEER will do about water quality 'on ship' being challenged. Read with its neighbours that is the POTABLE and domestic system, and the duty is MLC Regulation 3.2 and Standard A3.2.7. The card opens by splitting potable from technical water explicitly and tells the candidate to say which he means, so a candidate who meets the other reading in the room is not stranded. The two answers are NOT merged. AUG-0235 IS NOT ANSWERED. Identity resolution only, per section 13, and the outcome is RESOLVED_MEDIUM_REVIEW_REQUIRED, not a card. See the adjudication record. NO INVENTED NUMBERS. There is deliberately no ODMCS calibration interval, no MLC water-testing interval, and no universal PVC or sludge rule beyond what regulation 16 states. Where an instrument is silent the cards say so, because on all three of these subjects the confident invented number is the common wrong answer. INDEPENDENT REVIEW - THREE BLOCKING FINDINGS, ALL VERIFIED BY THE PRODUCER AT SOURCE AND ALL APPLIED. (1) QB3_C#q7 gave MEPC.328(76) as in force 1 NOVEMBER 2023. The resolution's own operative paragraph 3 reads 'shall enter into force on 1 November 2022', with deemed acceptance 1 May 2022 at paragraph 2. Corrected in three places. THE SOURCE OF THE ERROR MATTERS MORE THAN THE ERROR: the card took the date from the corpus's own frozen MARPOL Annex VI canonical layer, which records 2023-11-01. That layer is ours, it is qualified and frozen, and it is wrong on a date the underlying PDF states in one line. A corpus referral is raised; the defect is corpus-wide, not card-local, and any card authored off that layer inherits it. Recorded as known trap 59. (2) QB3_F#q11 asserted that MEPC.240(65) 'does not change section 5'. False: item 7 adds a new 5.7 requiring maker-recommended ODME spares to be carried, and item 8 renumbers the existing 5.7 as 5.8. The calibration provisions 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.5 are untouched so the headline answer survives, but a stated negative was false and the records citation has moved to 5.6 and 5.8. (3) QB4_H#q14 said food and drinking water is one of FOURTEEN areas subject to MLC inspection. Appendix A5-I lists SIXTEEN, and the heading is 'Food and catering', not drinking water. Corrected. NON-BLOCKING APPLIED: the reg. 16 unamended claim scoped to the held in-force chain; reg. 31.1's 'subject to regulation 3.4 and 3.5' exemption limb restored; UR Z20 3.1.2 and 3.1.3 separated from 3.1.1; the UR's printed 'filling procedures' typo marked rather than silently corrected; and MLC Reg. 3.2(1)'s cultural and religious clause restored. REVIEWER CLAIMS VERIFIED AS CORRECT AND NOT DISPUTED: every reg. 16 prohibition and temperature, the 16.4 reading that MARPOL imposes no blanket in-port incinerator ban, the absence of any calibration interval in reg. 31, the verbatim MEPC.108(49) 5.3 quotation, all UR Z20 sub-paragraphs including the certificate name, and every MLC quotation. QB1_F#q23 was ACCEPTED with no blocking defect.

cards.topic: Shipboard incineration - MARPOL Annex VI reg. 16: incinerator-only rule, the six prohibited substances, PVC conditional on IMO Type Approval, the sludge/boiler exception and its ports-harbours-estuaries limit, appendix IV approval from 1 January 2000, manual, training and the 850/600 degree temperature regime
cards.adjudication_note: Eleven cards mention an incinerator and none states its regulatory regime; searches for 'Annex VI reg 16', 'shipboard incinerator' and 'MEPC.244' return zero across the live bank. All eleven mentions are contextual - London Convention, Annex V records, IOPP checklist, carbon footprint.

cards.topic: ODMCS calibration - that MARPOL sets no interval; reg. 31 approval, recording, three-year retention, automatic stopping and the one-ballast-voyage concession; and MEPC.108(49) section 5 - verification at the IOPP renewal survey, calibration certificate on board, maker-only seals, and the onboard drift and re-zero checks
cards.adjudication_note: QB3_F#q3 gives the reg. 34 discharge criteria the ODMCS enforces and names the ODME in its tag line, but treats it as a compliance item, not as a maintained and verified instrument. Ten cards mention ODME/ODMCS and none addresses calibration. AUG-0102, an earlier August ask for the discharge criteria enforced by the ODMCS, is correctly held as PARAPHRASE_EXISTING against QB3_F#q3 and is NOT re-adjudicated here - the two asks are different halves.

cards.topic: PMS approval certificate - the company PMS under ISM s.10 distinguished from the class-approved Planned Maintenance Scheme under IACS UR Z20; the Certificate of Approval for Planned Maintenance Scheme or equivalent class notation kept on board; the CE named as responsible person; approval documentation; implementation survey within one year, annual audit, and the society's power to cancel
cards.adjudication_note: Five title-bearing survey cards were read in full. QB1_F#q14 gives survey types and CSM; QB1_F#q15 what a CE may not credit; QB1_supplementary#q4 the CMS scope; QB4_B#q3 the ISM s.10 maintenance obligation; QB1_G#q40 CSM. None answers 'what certificate will be onboard', and none names UR Z20 or the certificate. The new card cross-links all of them rather than restating them.

cards.topic: Fresh-water quality challenged - potable and domestic water distinguished from technical water; MLC Reg. 3.2 and Std A3.2.2(a) and A3.2.7; the WHO Guide to Ship Sanitation as guidance; and the CE's action as contain, diagnose across production, bunkering, storage and distribution, then restore and record
cards.adjudication_note: QB4_H#q9 was read in full: it is the WHO/IHR CERTIFICATE card - SSCC, SSCEC, Maritime Declaration of Health - and it states in one line that potable water quality is verified against the WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality. It does not answer what the CE does when quality is challenged. Two cards mention 'potable' and six 'drinking water', all in MLC-welfare or certificate contexts. The new card cross-links q9 rather than repeating the certificate set.
